{{Tooltip|W|Won}} 85–77 {{Abbr|OT|Overtime}} vs. [[2018–19 Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball team|Texas Tech]] | off_scheme = [[Blocker-Mover offense|Blocker-Mover]] | def_scheme = [[Glossary of basketball terms#P|Pack-Line]] |captain = [[Jack Salt]] |captain2 = [[Kyle Guy]] |captain3 = [[Ty Jerome]] }} {{2018–19 ACC men's basketball standings}} The '''2018–19 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Virginia]] during the [[2018–19 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The team was led by head coach [[Tony Bennett (basketball, born 1969)|Tony Bennett]] in his tenth year, and played their home games at [[John Paul Jones Arena]] in [[Charlottesville, Virginia]] as members of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]]. UVA opened the season with consecutive wins over ranked [[Big Ten]] teams, No. 25 Wisconsin ([[Battle 4 Atlantis#2018|Battle 4 Atlantis]]) and No. 24 Maryland ([[ACC–Big Ten Challenge]]), the latter of which improved Bennett's record in the Challenge to 8–2. An unheralded [[2018–19 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team#2018 recruiting class|two-star]] recruit, 5'9" [[Kihei Clark]] from [[Los Angeles, California]], started both games as a true freshman. The team then started the season 16–0 before falling to No. 1 Duke, 72–70.[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401082681 RJ Barrett leads No. 1 Duke past No. 4 Virginia 72–70], accessed January 19, 2019 The game was just the fourth in college basketball history between two teams both ranked No. 1, as the No. 4 Cavaliers were voted atop the Coaches Poll before the loss. After a 16–2 ACC record, Virginia won a share of their fourth ACC regular season title in the past six years.{{cite news|last=Wang|first=Gene|date=9 March 2019|title=Virginia basketball clinches ACC title share, but honoring Jack Salt was 'more important'|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/colleges/virginia-basketball-clinches-acc-title-share-but-honoring-jack-salt-was-more-important/2019/03/09/397b5362-42b8-11e9-9361-301ffb5bd5e6_story.html|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|location=Charlottesville, Virginia, USA|access-date=11 March 2019}} In the ACC tournament, the Cavaliers defeated NC State 76–56, before falling to Florida State in the conference semifinals. Virginia was then awarded the No. 1 seed in the South region and dispatched Gardner-Webb and Oklahoma by healthy margins in the first two rounds in [[Columbia, South Carolina]]. They advanced to a Sweet 16 matchup with Oregon and beat Oregon 53–49 to advance to their 2nd Elite 8 under Bennett. In the Elite Eight, they beat Purdue 80–75 in overtime to secure a trip to their first Final Four since 1984. On April 6, 2019, they defeated Auburn in their Final Four matchup by a score of 63–62 on 3 last-second free throws by [[Kyle Guy]], cementing the program's first ever trip to the national championship game.{{cite news | url=https://www.ncaa.com/news/basketball-men/article/2019-04-06/virginia-auburn-score-kyle-guy-free-throws-send-cavaliers | title=Kyle Guy's free throws with 0.6 seconds remaining send Virginia to the title game | newspaper=Ncaa.com }} On April 8, 2019, Virginia beat Texas Tech 85–77 in overtime, winning its first national championship. ==Previous season== Unranked by the AP in the preseason poll, the [[2017–18 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|Cavaliers]] surprisingly finished the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2017–18 season]] 31–3, and 17–1 [[2017–18 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|in ACC play]] to win both ACC Regular Season and tournament titles. The Cavaliers received an automatic bid to the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 1 seed in the South region, [[2018 Virginia vs. UMBC men's basketball game|where they were upset by No. 16]] [[2017–18 UMBC Retrievers men's basketball team|UMBC]] in the [[2018 UMBC vs. Virginia men's basketball game|first round]]. This was the first time in Men's NCAA tournament history that a No. 1 seed was upset by a No. 16 seed. ==Offseason== Virginia's offseason started on the night of March 16, 2018, and ended on the evening of November 6, 2018.
